records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: Yahweh spoke to Moses: the command for the ordination given in Exodus 29
decisions.reason: Chapters 8-9 carry out what God commanded in Exodus 29:1-37 and 40:12-15: the washing, clothing and anointing of Aaron and his sons and the seven days of their ordination. The account follows those commands step by step, and again and again says that it was done "as Yahweh had commanded Moses".

records.heading: Aaron and his sons are ordained

records.source: קַ֤ח אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו אִתּ֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ הַבְּגָדִ֔ים וְאֵ֖ת שֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֑ה וְאֵ֣ת׀פַּ֣ר הַֽחַטָּ֗את וְאֵת֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הָֽאֵילִ֔ים וְאֵ֖ת סַ֥ל הַמַּצּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments and the oil of the anointing and the bull of the sin offering and the two rams and the basket of the unleavened [bread],
pieces: "Take Aaron, and his sons with him. Take also the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread made without yeast.

L.2: "Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the oil of anointing, and the bull of the sin offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened [bread],

R.2: "Bring Aaron and his sons. Also bring the priests' clothes, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread made without yeast.

decisions.choice: the garments: the priestly clothing made in Exodus 28 and 39
decisions.reason: "The garments" are the holy garments God commanded for Aaron and his sons "for glory and for beauty" (Exodus 28:2, 40), made in Exodus 39:1-31. Verses 7-9 and 13 list them.

decisions.choice: the oil of anointing: the holy oil mixed by a set recipe
decisions.reason: This is the sacred oil of Exodus 30:22-33, olive oil blended with myrrh, cinnamon, fragrant cane and cassia. It was used only to anoint the tabernacle, its furnishings and the priests, and no one was to make it for any other use. To anoint was to pour or smear oil on a person or thing to mark it as set apart for God (verses 10-12).

decisions.choice: the two rams and the basket: the offerings of Exodus 29:1-3
decisions.reason: Exodus 29:1-3 names the same animals and the basket of bread. One ram is a burnt offering (verses 18-21) and the other the ram of ordination (verse 22). For the sin offering see 4:3; for unleavened bread see 2:4.

decisions.choice: the priests' clothes
decisions.reason: Readable says whose garments they are. Balanced and Literal keep "the garments", which the reader knows from Exodus 28.

records.source: וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־הָעֵדָ֖ה הַקְהֵ֑ל אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: and all the congregation assemble to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: Then call the whole congregation together at the entrance of the tent of meeting."

L.3: and assemble all the congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting."

R.3: Then gather all the people of the community at the entrance of the meeting tent."

decisions.choice: the congregation: the whole people of Israel gathered as a body
decisions.reason: The word names Israel as a community that meets together (4:13; Exodus 12:3). The whole people is to watch the ordination of its priests; in verse 4 they gather.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the tent of meeting: the courtyard in front of the tent
decisions.reason: The open space in the courtyard before the tent, where the altar of burnt offering stood (Exodus 40:6, 29). See the note on the tent of meeting at 1:1.

decisions.choice: congregation (Balanced); the people of the community (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the more common word "community" and says that it is made of people.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ וַתִּקָּהֵל֙ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And did Moses just as commanded Yahweh him, and assembled the congregation to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: Moses followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, and the congregation gathered at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

L.4: And Moses did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, and the congregation assembled at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

R.4: Moses obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the people of the community came together at the entrance of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: Moses did as Yahweh commanded: the ordination follows God's word exactly
decisions.reason: This formula runs through the chapter (verses 9, 13, 17, 21, 29, 36), as it does through the making of the tabernacle (Exodus 39:1-43; 40:16-33). Nothing in the rite is of Moses' own devising.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הָעֵדָ֑ה זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to the congregation, this [is] the thing which commanded Yahweh to do.
pieces: Moses said to the congregation, "What you are about to see done is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."

L.5: And Moses said to the congregation, "This [is] the thing which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded to do."

R.5: Moses told the people, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded us to do what you will now see."

decisions.choice: this is the thing: what follows, the rite about to be performed
decisions.reason: "The thing" (literally "the word") points forward to the actions of verses 6-35. Moses tells the people that what they will watch is God's command, not his own plan.

decisions.choice: what you are about to see done (Balanced); what you will now see (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "to do". Balanced and Readable make clear that the people are watching the rite that follows.

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵ֣ב מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑יו וַיִּרְחַ֥ץ אֹתָ֖ם בַּמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And brought near Moses Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.
pieces: Moses had Aaron and his sons come forward, and he washed them with water.

L.6: And Moses brought Aaron and his sons near and washed them with water.

R.6: Moses had Aaron and his sons come forward. He washed them with water.

decisions.choice: washed them with water: a washing before they put on the holy garments
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 29:4 and 40:12, the priests are washed before they are clothed and anointed. The washing makes them ready to come near the holy things. Later the priests were to wash their hands and feet each time they served (Exodus 30:19-21).

decisions.choice: brought near: had them come forward
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for bringing an offering near (1:2). Here Moses brings Aaron and his sons forward to the entrance of the tent.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן עָלָ֜יו אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּ֗נֶת וַיַּחְגֹּ֤ר אֹתוֹ֙ בָּֽאַבְנֵ֔ט וַיַּלְבֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶֽת־הַמְּעִ֔יל וַיִּתֵּ֥ן עָלָ֖יו אֶת־הָאֵפֹ֑ד וַיַּחְגֹּ֣ר אֹת֗וֹ בְּחֵ֨שֶׁב֙ הָֽאֵפֹ֔ד וַיֶּאְפֹּ֥ד ל֖וֹ בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And put on him the tunic and girded him with the sash and clothed him [with] the robe and put on him the ephod and girded him with [the] band of the ephod and bound [it] to him with it.
pieces: He put the tunic on Aaron and tied the sash around his waist. He dressed him in the robe and put the ephod over it, then tied the ephod's woven band around him, and so fastened the ephod on him.

L.7: And he put the tunic on him and tied the sash around him, and clothed him [with] the robe, and put the ephod on him, and tied the band of the ephod around him and bound [the ephod] on him with it.

R.7: He put the tunic on Aaron and tied the sash around his waist. He dressed him in the robe. Then he put the ephod on him. This was a special vest. Moses tied it on him with its woven belt.

decisions.choice: the tunic, the sash, the robe: the high priest's clothing from the skin out
decisions.reason: The tunic was a long shirt of fine linen worn next to the body (Exodus 28:39); the sash was a woven belt tied around it (Exodus 39:29). Over these went the robe, all of blue, with pomegranates and gold bells around its hem (Exodus 28:31-35). Moses dresses Aaron in the order Exodus 29:5 gives.

decisions.choice: the ephod and its band: the high priest's outer vest and its waistband
decisions.reason: The ephod was the outermost garment of the high priest, made of gold, blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, held by shoulder pieces that carried two onyx stones engraved with the names of the tribes (Exodus 28:6-12). Its band, woven in one piece with it, tied it around the waist. Its exact shape is not described; it seems to have been a kind of vest or apron.

decisions.choice: bound it on him with it: the band fastened the ephod to his body
decisions.reason: The last verb is formed from the word "ephod" itself: he "ephod-ed" him with the band, that is, he fastened the ephod on him by tying the band.

decisions.choice: This was a special vest.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ephod, a word most readers will not know, in a short added sentence. The comparison to a vest is approximate.

records.source: וַיָּ֥שֶׂם עָלָ֖יו אֶת־הַחֹ֑שֶׁן וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶל־הַחֹ֔שֶׁן אֶת־הָאוּרִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַתֻּמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And placed on him the breastpiece, and put in the breastpiece the Urim and the Thummim.
pieces: Over it he set the breastpiece, and inside the breastpiece he placed the Urim and the Thummim.

L.8: And he placed the breastpiece on him, and in the breastpiece he put the Urim and the Thummim.

R.8: He put the breastpiece on Aaron's chest. Inside it he placed the Urim and Thummim. These were used to learn what God wanted.

decisions.choice: the breastpiece: a square pouch worn on the chest, set with twelve stones
decisions.reason: Exodus 28:15-30 describes it: a square of the same woven work as the ephod, folded double, set with twelve gems engraved with the names of the tribes, and fastened to the ephod with gold chains and rings. It is called "the breastpiece of judgment" because it held the Urim and Thummim (Exodus 28:15, 30).

decisions.choice: the Urim and the Thummim: objects kept in the breastpiece for seeking God's decision
decisions.reason: Scripture never describes them. They were used to ask God for a decision when Israel needed guidance (Numbers 27:21; Deuteronomy 33:8; 1 Samuel 28:6; Ezra 2:63). The names may mean "lights" and "perfections", but how they were used, perhaps as lots giving a yes or no, is not known. The names are kept as they are.

decisions.choice: These were used to learn what God wanted.
decisions.reason: Readable adds a short explanation of the Urim and Thummim from Numbers 27:21. It says no more than Scripture does about how they worked.

records.source: וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־הַמִּצְנֶ֖פֶת עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיָּ֨שֶׂם עַֽל־הַמִּצְנֶ֜פֶת אֶל־מ֣וּל פָּנָ֗יו אֵ֣ת צִ֤יץ הַזָּהָב֙ נֵ֣זֶר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And placed the turban on his head, and placed on the turban to [the] front of his face the plate of the gold, [the] crown of the holiness, just as commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: He set the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban he fixed the gold plate, the holy crown, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.9: And he placed the turban on his head, and he placed on the turban, on its front, the plate of gold, the crown of holiness, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.9: He put the turban on Aaron's head. On the front of the turban he fastened the gold plate. It was the holy crown, the sign that Aaron belonged to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Moses did this just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

decisions.choice: the turban: the high priest's headdress of fine linen
decisions.reason: A head covering wound of fine linen (Exodus 28:39; 39:28), worn only by the high priest. His sons wear a different headdress (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the plate of gold, the crown of holiness: a gold plate engraved "Holy to Yahweh"
decisions.reason: The first word may mean a flower or shining thing; it is the plate of pure gold tied with a blue cord on the front of the turban and engraved "Holy to Yahweh" (Exodus 28:36-38; 39:30-31). It is called a crown, a word for a sign of consecration from the same root as "Nazirite" (Numbers 6:7). It marked Aaron as set apart, bearing the guilt of the holy gifts of Israel (Exodus 28:38).

decisions.choice: the sign that Aaron belonged to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the holy crown" from the words engraved on it in Exodus 28:36.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה וַיִּמְשַׁ֥ח אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֑וֹ וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And took Moses [the] oil of the anointing and anointed the tabernacle and all that [was] in it and consecrated them.
pieces: Moses then took the anointing oil. He anointed the tabernacle and all that it held, and consecrated them.

L.10: And Moses took the oil of anointing and anointed the tabernacle and all that [was] in it, and consecrated them.

R.10: Then Moses took the anointing oil. He poured some on the tabernacle and everything in it. In this way he set them apart as holy.

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy, set apart for God alone
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something holy: to move it out of common use into God's own possession and service. What is consecrated belongs to God and must be handled as he directs. Holy is not the same as clean: a clean thing is fit for common use, while a holy thing is no longer common at all (10:10). Here the anointing is the act that consecrates the tabernacle, its furnishings, the altar and the priests (verses 11-12, 30; Exodus 29:44; 40:9-13). The same verb is used of God making Israel holy (20:8; 22:32). What God has made holy can be profaned, treated as common (19:8; 22:2).

decisions.choice: anointed the tabernacle: smeared or sprinkled with the holy oil
decisions.reason: The tabernacle is the dwelling, the tent itself with its frames and curtains (Exodus 26). Anointing it and its furnishings was commanded in Exodus 30:26-29 and 40:9-11, which says that they become most holy and make holy whatever touches them.

decisions.choice: set them apart as holy
decisions.reason: Readable explains "consecrate", a word many readers do not use, as "set apart as holy". Literal and Balanced keep "consecrate". The same wording is used wherever this verb means making a thing or person holy.

decisions.choice: poured some on
decisions.reason: Readable describes what anointing was, putting oil on a thing. Literal and Balanced keep "anointed".

records.source: וַיַּ֥ז מִמֶּ֛נּוּ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וַיִּמְשַׁ֨ח אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֗יו וְאֶת־הַכִּיֹּ֛ר וְאֶת־כַּנּ֖וֹ לְקַדְּשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times and anointed the altar and all its utensils and the basin and its stand, to consecrate them.
pieces: He sprinkled some of the oil seven times on the altar, and anointed the altar with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.

L.11: And he sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand, to consecrate them.

R.11: He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and all the tools used with it. He also anointed the large bowl for washing and its stand. He did this to set them apart as holy.

decisions.choice: sprinkled seven times: spattered drops of oil, seven being a number of completeness
decisions.reason: This verb means to spatter in small drops (4:6), not to throw or splash. Seven sprinklings mark the act as full and complete, as with blood in 4:6 and 16:14, 19. Exodus 29:36-37 commands that the altar be made holy over seven days.

decisions.choice: the altar ... the basin and its stand: the bronze altar of burnt offering and the bronze basin
decisions.reason: The altar is the altar of burnt offering in the courtyard (Exodus 27:1-8); its utensils are its pots, shovels, basins, forks and fire pans (Exodus 27:3). The basin stood between the tent and the altar and held water for the priests' washing (Exodus 30:17-21). Consecrate: see verse 10.

decisions.choice: the large bowl for washing
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the basin was for, as Exodus 30:18-19 says.

records.source: וַיִּצֹק֙ מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ אַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיִּמְשַׁ֥ח אֹת֖וֹ לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: And poured some of [the] oil of the anointing on [the] head of Aaron and anointed him to consecrate him.
pieces: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head, anointing him to consecrate him.

L.12: And he poured some of the oil of anointing on Aaron's head and anointed him, to consecrate him.

R.12: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head. He anointed him to set him apart as holy.

decisions.choice: poured on Aaron's head: Aaron is anointed as high priest
decisions.reason: Oil is poured on Aaron's head, not only sprinkled. Exodus 29:7 commanded this, and Psalm 133:2 remembers the oil running down on Aaron's beard and collar. Aaron becomes "the anointed priest" (4:3, 5, 16; 6:15). His sons are sprinkled with oil and blood later (verse 30; Exodus 29:21).

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵ֨ב מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁ֤ם כֻּתֳּנֹת֙ וַיַּחְגֹּ֤ר אֹתָם֙ אַבְנֵ֔ט וַיַּחֲבֹ֥שׁ לָהֶ֖ם מִגְבָּע֑וֹת כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And brought near Moses [the] sons of Aaron and clothed them [with] tunics and girded them [with] a sash and bound on them caps, just as commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: Then Moses had Aaron's sons come forward. He dressed them in tunics, tied sashes around their waists, and fastened caps on their heads, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.13: And Moses brought Aaron's sons near and clothed them [with] tunics, and tied sashes around them, and bound caps on them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.13: Next Moses brought Aaron's sons forward. He put tunics on them and tied sashes around their waists. He put caps on their heads. He did it just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

decisions.choice: tunics, sashes and caps: the clothing of the ordinary priests
decisions.reason: Aaron's sons wear the simpler garments of Exodus 28:40-43, made "for glory and for beauty": a linen tunic, a sash and a headdress. The word for their headdress differs from Aaron's turban (verse 9); it may describe a rounded cap or a band wound around the head (Exodus 39:28).

decisions.choice: sashes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular "a sash", meaning one for each son. English says "sashes". In Literal the plural needs no bracket, since no word is added.

records.source: וַיַּגֵּ֕שׁ אֵ֖ת פַּ֣ר הַֽחַטָּ֑את וַיִּסְמֹ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּבָנָיו֙ אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֔ם עַל־רֹ֖אשׁ פַּ֥ר הַֽחַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And brought near the bull of the sin offering, and leaned Aaron and his sons their hands on [the] head of [the] bull of the sin offering.
pieces: He led up the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

L.14: And he brought near the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons leaned their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.

R.14: Then Moses brought the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.

decisions.choice: leaned their hands on the head: Aaron and his sons make the offering their own
decisions.reason: As in 1:4 and 4:4, leaning the hand on the animal marks it as the offering of the one who brings it. Here the new priests offer first for themselves: before they can make atonement for others, atonement is made for them (verse 34; 9:7; Hebrews 7:27). For the sin offering see 4:3.

decisions.choice: its head
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "its head" rather than repeat "the bull of the sin offering".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁחָ֗ט וַיִּקַּ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־הַדָּם֙ וַ֠יִּתֵּן עַל־קַרְנ֨וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֤חַ סָבִיב֙ בְּאֶצְבָּע֔וֹ וַיְחַטֵּ֖א אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְאֶת־הַדָּ֗ם יָצַק֙ אֶל־יְס֣וֹד הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיְקַדְּשֵׁ֖הוּ לְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And slaughtered [it], and took Moses the blood and put [it] on [the] horns of the altar all around with his finger, and purified the altar, and the blood poured out at [the] base of the altar, and consecrated it to make atonement on it.
pieces: Moses slaughtered it, took the blood, and with his finger put some on each of the horns of the altar all around, purifying the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. So he consecrated it, to make atonement for it.

L.15: And he slaughtered [it], and Moses took the blood and put [it] on the horns of the altar all around with his finger, and purified the altar; and the blood he poured out at the base of the altar, and he consecrated it, to make atonement for it.

R.15: Moses killed the bull. He took its blood and used his finger to put some on all the horns at the corners of the altar. In this way he made the altar pure. He poured out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. So he set the altar apart as holy and made atonement for it.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: most likely Moses, named with the next verb
decisions.reason: The first verb has no stated subject; Moses is named with the second. Exodus 29:10-11 tells Moses to slaughter the bull, so Moses is most likely the subject of both. The same pattern recurs in verses 19 and 23.

decisions.choice: purified the altar: cleansed it from sin's defilement
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "sin offering". It means to remove the stain of sin, to purify. The blood of the sin offering cleanses the altar, as in Exodus 29:36-37, so that it can be holy and used for atonement. See the note on the sin offering at 4:3.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for it: for the altar itself
decisions.reason: "On it" here means for the altar, which is cleansed and consecrated so that atonement can be made on it from now on (Exodus 29:36-37). For atonement see 1:4; for the horns and the base see 4:7.

decisions.choice: all the horns at the corners of the altar
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the horns stood at the altar's four corners (Exodus 27:2).

decisions.reason: This word for fat appears only here, in verse 20, and in 1:8 and 1:12. It seems to mean the firm fat around the kidneys and loins, the suet.

decisions.choice: the whole ram ... a burnt offering: the ram is wholly given to Yahweh
decisions.reason: As with every burnt offering (1:9), the whole animal is burned. The words follow Exodus 29:18. For "soothing aroma" and "offering by fire" see 1:9.

R.22: Next he brought the second ram. It was the ram for ordaining the priests. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.

decisions.choice: the ram of ordination: literally "the ram of the fillings"
decisions.reason: The word means "fillings". It comes from the idiom "to fill the hand", used for installing someone as a priest (verse 33; Exodus 28:41; 29:9; Judges 17:5, 12). The idiom may come from putting parts of the offering into the priests' hands, as Moses does in verses 26-28, or from giving a man his priestly share and right to serve. This ram and its offering complete the priests' installation. Its rite is commanded in Exodus 29:19-34.

decisions.choice: ordination (Literal, Balanced); ordaining the priests (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Ordination" names what the offering does: it installs Aaron and his sons as priests. "Filling" would hide the meaning, so all three levels say "ordination", and Literal keeps the idiom where the verb "fill" itself appears (verse 33). Readable says what is being done and for whom.

L.23: And he slaughtered [it], and Moses took some of its blood and put [it] on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

R.23: Moses killed the ram and took some of its blood. He put it on Aaron's right earlobe, on his right thumb and on the big toe of his right foot.

decisions.choice: ear, thumb, big toe: the whole person set apart for God's service
decisions.reason: The blood is put on the extremities of the right side of the body, as Exodus 29:20 commands. The rite seems to mark the whole person, from head to foot, as cleansed and set apart. Some see the ear as hearing God's word, the hand as doing his work, and the foot as walking in his ways, but the text does not explain it. The same rite cleanses a person healed of skin disease (14:14, 17, 25, 28).

decisions.choice: their ear, their hand, their foot: each son's
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the singular with "their": the right ear, hand and foot of each son. The rite is the same as Aaron's in verse 23.

decisions.choice: lobes ... thumbs ... big toes
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plural for the several sons; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.reason: The fat parts are those of a sheep offered as a peace offering (3:9-10); the fat tail is the broad tail of the sheep (3:9). The right thigh is normally the priest's share of a peace offering (7:32-33). Here, at the ordination, it is not eaten by a priest but burned on the altar (verse 28; Exodus 29:22-25).

decisions.choice: He took the fat: the fat tail ...
decisions.reason: Balanced reads the first "the fat" as a heading for the fat parts that follow. Literal keeps the plain list.

decisions.choice: on the burnt offering: on top of the ram of verse 21

decisions.choice: the breast was Moses' portion: Moses acts as priest at the ordination
decisions.reason: Normally the breast of a peace offering belongs to the priests (7:30-31, 34). At this ordination Moses does the priest's work, so the breast is his share, as Exodus 29:26 commands. After this Aaron and his sons offer for themselves (9:1-24).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֜ה מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֗ה וּמִן־הַדָּם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ֒ וַיַּ֤ז עַֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ עַל־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְעַל־בָּנָ֛יו וְעַל־בִּגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וַיְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְאֶת־בָּנָ֛יו וְאֶת־בִּגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And took Moses some of [the] oil of the anointing and some of the blood which [was] on the altar and sprinkled [it] on Aaron, on his garments, and on his sons and on [the] garments of his sons with him, and consecrated Aaron, his garments, and his sons and [the] garments of his sons with him.
pieces: Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. In this way he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

L.30: And Moses took some of the oil of anointing and some of the blood that [was] on the altar and sprinkled [it] on Aaron, on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons with him; and he consecrated Aaron, his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him.

R.30: Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar. He sprinkled them on Aaron and his clothes, and on Aaron's sons and their clothes. In this way he set Aaron and his sons apart as holy, together with their clothes.

decisions.choice: oil and blood together: the priests are both cleansed and made holy
decisions.reason: Exodus 29:21 commands this sprinkling with both the oil and the blood from the altar. The blood from the altar joins the priests to the altar and its atonement, and the oil marks them as holy. Now the sons too are anointed (Exodus 28:41; 30:30; 40:15).

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. The garments too become holy, so that the priests' clothing is passed on to Aaron's successors at their own anointing (Exodus 29:29).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־אַהֲרֹ֣ן וְאֶל־בָּנָ֗יו בַּשְּׁל֣וּ אֶת־הַבָּשָׂר֮ פֶּ֣תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֒ וְשָׁם֙ תֹּאכְל֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וְאֶ֨ת־הַלֶּ֔חֶם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּסַ֣ל הַמִּלֻּאִ֑ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוֵּ֨יתִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַהֲרֹ֥ן וּבָנָ֖יו יֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Aaron and to his sons, boil the meat [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting, and there you will eat it and the bread which [is] in [the] basket of the ordination, just as I commanded, saying, Aaron and his sons will eat it.
pieces: Moses told Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting and eat it there, with the bread that is in the ordination basket, as I commanded when I said, 'Aaron and his sons are to eat it.'

L.31: And Moses said to Aaron and to his sons, "Boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and there you will eat it and the bread that [is] in the basket of the ordination [offerings], just as I commanded, saying, 'Aaron and his sons will eat it.'

R.31: Moses told Aaron and his sons, "Cook the meat at the entrance of the meeting tent. Eat it there with the bread from the basket for the ordination. That is what I commanded. I said, 'Aaron and his sons must eat it.'

decisions.choice: boil the meat and eat it there: the priests eat the rest of the ram of ordination
decisions.reason: The rest of the ram, apart from the parts burned and Moses' breast, is eaten by Aaron and his sons in the holy place, near the tent, with the remaining bread (Exodus 29:31-33). As with a peace offering, those for whom the sacrifice was made share its meal (7:15).

decisions.choice: I commanded: as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "I commanded": Moses refers to his own instruction, which repeated God's command. The Septuagint reads "as it was commanded to me", which matches verse 35, and the same consonants could be read "I was commanded".

decisions.choice: Cook
decisions.reason: Readable says "cook". The Hebrew word means to cook in water, to boil, which Literal and Balanced keep.

records.source: וְהַנּוֹתָ֥ר בַּבָּשָׂ֖ר וּבַלָּ֑חֶם בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשְׂרֹֽפוּ׃
records.gloss: And the remainder of the meat and of the bread with fire you will burn.
pieces: Whatever is left of the meat and the bread you must burn up.

L.32: And what is left over of the meat and of the bread you will burn with fire.

R.32: You must burn up any meat or bread that is left over.

decisions.choice: burn what is left: holy food may not be kept
decisions.reason: As Exodus 29:34 commands, what is not eaten is burned, not kept until later, "because it is holy". Compare the rule for the thanksgiving offering in 7:15-17.

records.source: וּמִפֶּתַח֩ אֹ֨הֶל מוֹעֵ֜ד לֹ֤א תֵֽצְאוּ֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים עַ֚ד י֣וֹם מְלֹ֔את יְמֵ֖י מִלֻּאֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת־יֶדְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And from [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting not you will go out [for] seven days, until [the] day [the] days of your ordination are complete, for seven days he will fill your hand.
pieces: Stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting and do not leave it for seven days, until the time of your ordination is over. It will take seven days for you to be ordained.

L.33: And from the entrance of the tent of meeting you will not go out [for] seven days, until the day the days of your ordination are completed; for seven days he will fill your hand.

R.33: Do not leave the entrance of the meeting tent for seven days. Stay until the days for making you priests are over. It will take seven days to make you priests.

decisions.choice: he will fill your hand: you will be ordained
alternatives: your ordination will take seven days
decisions.reason: "To fill the hand" means to install as priest (see verse 22). "He" is not named: it may be Yahweh, or Moses as the one performing the rite, or it may be impersonal, "your hand will be filled".

decisions.choice: seven days: the rite is repeated each day for a week
decisions.reason: Exodus 29:35-37 commands that the ordination and the purifying of the altar be done each day for seven days. Seven days is also the time for other passages from one state to another, such as cleansing from uncleanness (12:2; 14:8-9; 15:13). The new priests stay in the holy area all that time (verse 35).

decisions.choice: for you to be ordained (Balanced); to make you priests (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom. Literal keeps "fill your hand".

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לַעֲשֹׂ֖ת לְכַפֵּ֥ר עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Just as one has done on this day, has commanded Yahweh to do, to make atonement for you.
pieces: What has been done today, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded to be done again, to make atonement for you.

L.34: As has been done this day, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded to do, to make atonement for you.

R.34: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded that what was done today be done each day. It will make atonement for you.

decisions.choice: as has been done today ... Yahweh has commanded to do: the same rite is to be repeated on each of the seven days
alternatives: Yahweh commanded what has been done today
decisions.reason: The sentence is compressed. It most likely means that what was done on this first day is what Yahweh has commanded to be done for the seven days of verse 33 (Exodus 29:35-36). It could also simply mean that what was done today was done at Yahweh's command.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for you: the priests themselves need atonement
decisions.reason: The ordination makes atonement for Aaron and his sons. Before they serve as priests for others, their own sin must be dealt with (verse 14; 9:7). For atonement see 1:4.

decisions.choice: again (Balanced); each day (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the reading of the decision above explicit.

records.source: וּפֶתַח֩ אֹ֨הֶל מוֹעֵ֜ד תֵּשְׁב֨וּ יוֹמָ֤ם וָלַ֨יְלָה֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֛ם אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תָמ֑וּתוּ כִּי־כֵ֖ן צֻוֵּֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: And [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting you will stay day and night [for] seven days, and you will keep the charge of Yahweh, and not you will die, for so I have been commanded.
pieces: Remain at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days, and keep the watch {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you, so that you will not die. This is the command I have received."

L.35: And at the entrance of the tent of meeting you will stay day and night [for] seven days, and you will keep the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that you will not die; for so I have been commanded."

R.35: Stay at the entrance of the meeting tent day and night for seven days. Do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told you to do. Then you will not die. That is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded me."

decisions.choice: keep the charge of Yahweh: carry out the duty Yahweh has given
decisions.reason: To keep a charge is to stand guard over a duty that has been entrusted (Numbers 3:7-8; 9:19). Here it means staying at the tent and doing all that the ordination requires. The new priests are in a state between the common and the holy, and leaving would put them in danger.

decisions.choice: so that you will not die: the holy is dangerous when it is not respected
decisions.reason: To disobey in dealing with the holy is deadly (10:2, 7; Exodus 28:35, 43). The warning prepares for the death of Nadab and Abihu in 10:1-2.

decisions.choice: what the LORD commanded me
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who gave the command, the LORD, which the passive "I have been commanded" implies.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אַהֲרֹ֖ן וּבָנָ֑יו אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And did Aaron and his sons all the things which commanded Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.
pieces: Aaron and his sons carried out everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses.

L.36: And Aaron and his sons did all the things that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded by the hand of Moses.

R.36: Aaron and his sons did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means "through", by means of a messenger. The chapter ends as it ran: everything was done as commanded (verse 4). The obedience of the new priests stands in contrast with 10:1, where two of them offer what was not commanded.
